model.rationale: Markets price Mannion near 95%, his fundraising edge over Buller is about seven to one, and the district's Democratic lean plus a favorable environment point to a comfortable margin; the expected edge is tempered somewhat because no public polls are available.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against Mannion or new polling showing a single-digit race would be the main signal of movement.

overview:
NY-22, anchored in central New York, leans Democratic on paper, and first-term incumbent John Mannion enters the general election with clear structural advantages. He has raised about $3.1 million and holds roughly $1.4 million on hand, dwarfing Republican Kailee Buller's $429,000 raised and $200,000 in cash. No outside groups have targeted the seat, and no expert raters list it as competitive.

Prediction markets on both Kalshi and Polymarket price Mannion around 94-95%, and the district's partisan lean combined with a favorable national environment points to a solid Democratic margin. With no public general-election polling available, some uncertainty remains about the precise size of the lead, but incumbency, money, and market pricing all make an upset a long shot.
